reason: The bone framework has spaces awaiting mineral, and the goal says to strengthen it.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the bone framework.

alternatives.reason: Building a muscle also matches a current goal.

effect: Mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the elbow joint movable; the next goal is to attach both muscles.
reaction: The distinction between hard bone and the movable joint is useful.
reason: The goal calls for muscles made from muscle cells and supporting tissue, so I’ll start with the front group.
expectation: The cells and supporting tissue should form a front upper-arm muscle.

alternatives.reason: I could build the back muscle first instead.

effect: The front cells and supporting tissue formed a biceps, with tendon ends for attachment.
reaction: The picture makes the connection from cells to a whole muscle clearer.
reason: The back muscle still needs to be built, and the same pairing worked for the front muscle.
expectation: The back cells and supporting tissue should form the back upper-arm muscle.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the front muscle before building the back one.

effect: Both muscles are built; their tendon ends show where they can attach to the skeleton.
reaction: The matching cutaways make the front and back muscles easy to compare.
reason: The biceps outline shows it crossing the front of the elbow, matching the goal to attach the muscles.
expectation: The biceps should attach to the front of the arm skeleton.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the back muscle first instead.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow, where its pull bends the forearm; the triceps still needs attaching.
reaction: The arrows make the bending action clearer.
reason: The triceps belongs on the back of the same arm, opposite the attached biceps.
expectation: The triceps should attach across the back of the elbow.

effect: The completed arm shows how muscles on opposite sides pull to bend and straighten the elbow. All goals are complete.
reaction: The two views made the muscles’ different jobs clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile because the two views showed why both muscles are needed: each pulls in a different direction.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the second muscle felt somewhat repetitive after using the same pairing for the first, although the matching pictures helped compare them.

surprise.text: I found it useful that mineral hardens the bone while the joint tissues stay free to move.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary; the goals and pictures explained the pairings.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter because seeing the finished arm connect muscle pulls to movement was interesting, even though some assembly steps were predictable.
